# Sirach Chapter 39 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 39 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_039_page_001.jpg

---

**39:1** But there is another kind of person: the scholar who dedicates himself to studying the Most High's instruction. Such a person searches out the wisdom of every ancient generation and pays close attention to prophecy.

**39:2** He preserves the teachings of great thinkers and probes the deeper meanings of figurative speech.

**39:3** He searches out the hidden truths in proverbs and puzzles over the riddles embedded in parables.

**39:4** He works among people of influence and presents himself before rulers. He travels through foreign lands, learning first-hand what is good and what is harmful in human experience.

**39:5** He is determined to rise early and seek the Lord his Maker; he prays before the Most High, opens his mouth in confession, and asks forgiveness for his sins.

**39:6** If the great Lord wills it, this person will be filled with the spirit of discernment. He will pour forth his own words of wisdom and offer his thanks to the Lord in prayer.

**39:7** He will develop sound judgment and deep knowledge, and he will meditate on God's hidden purposes.

**39:8** He will teach what he has discovered and find his pride and joy in the Lord's covenant instruction.

**39:9** Many people will celebrate his wisdom; it will never be forgotten. Generation after generation, his name will endure.

**39:10** Nations will speak of his wisdom; whole congregations will sing his praise.

**39:11** If he lives to old age, he will leave behind a legacy greater than a thousand others. And if he dies, he goes content.

**39:12** I still have more to say — I've been thinking it over, and I'm filled to the brim like the full moon.

**39:13** Listen to me, you people of God! Bud like a rose beside a running stream.

**39:14** Spread your fragrance like incense; blossom like a lily. Lift your voices and sing; bless the Lord for everything he has made.

**39:15** Give glory to his name; praise him with songs and with stringed instruments. This is what you will say when you give thanks:

**39:16** "Every work of the Lord is very good. All his commands will be carried out at exactly the right time."

**39:17** Don't ask, "What is this?" or "Why is that?" — everything will be understood in its time. At his command, the waters stood up in a heap; the great reservoirs of water obeyed his spoken word.

**39:18** Whatever he wills comes to pass with a word. Nothing can stop his saving work.

**39:19** Every human action lies exposed before him. Nothing is hidden from his sight.

**39:20** He sees from age to age; nothing surprises him.

**39:21** Don't ask, "What is this?" or "Why is that?" — everything was made with a purpose.

**39:22** His blessing flows over the dry land like a river; it saturates the earth like a flood.

**39:23** Just as he can turn a fertile land into salt wasteland, his anger strips the nations of their inheritance.

**39:24** For the righteous, his paths are smooth and easy; for the wicked, they are full of pitfalls.

**39:25** From the very beginning, good things were made for good people, and harmful things were made for sinners.

**39:26** The basic necessities of life are water, fire, iron, salt, grain, milk, honey, wine, oil, and clothing.

**39:27** For those who live rightly, all these things are blessings. But in the hands of sinners, they become instruments of harm.

**39:28** There are destructive winds God created as instruments of punishment; in their rage they can flatten mountains. At the time of devastation they unleash their power and bring God's anger to its completion.

**39:29** Fire, hail, famine, plague — all created as means of punishment.

**39:30** Wild beasts with their fangs, scorpions, vipers, and the punishing sword — all designed to destroy the wicked.

**39:31** All of these gladly obey his commands; they are stationed on earth ready for service; when their time comes, they will be there.

**39:32** So, from the very beginning I have been convinced — and after careful thought I have put this in writing:

**39:33** All the works of the Lord are good. He meets every need at the right time.

**39:34** No one can rightly say, "This is worse than that" — everything will prove its goodness in its own season.

**39:35** Now sing to the Lord with everything you have — with every breath and every voice. Bless the name of the Lord.
